## 3. The evidence that moved it

**"Virtual cell" is in a *Cell* title in December 2024.** [39672099](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39672099/): how to
build the virtual cell with artificial intelligence — priorities and
opportunities. This corpus has now dated the arrival of that vocabulary three
times: 2025-11, then 2025-04 after the first backfill, and now 2024-12. Each
date was the earliest month then being read. The honest conclusion is not a
fourth date but the retirement of the question.

**AI agents reach an oncology journal in December 2024, not June 2025.**
[39690222](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39690222/) (*Nat Cancer*): how AI agents will change cancer research and
oncology, published in the same issue as [39690213](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39690213/), foundation models in
clinical oncology. The corpus's dated diffusion chain — general and methods
bench in February 2025, oncology in June, immunology in December, "ten months"
— is wrong at its origin and wrong at its oncology waypoint. Both move back
about six months, and the lag it measured was an artefact of where reading began.

**Agents doing production work.** [39718779](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39718779/): an LLM-assisted workflow mines
thousands of enzyme-substrate interactions from published manuscripts. Not a
demonstration and not a benchmark — a literature-scale extraction job.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

Nothing lands on a tracked thread this month.

### (b) Method credibility

[39313595](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39313595/) (*Nat Med*): a toolbox for surfacing health-equity harms and
biases in large language models. December 2024 has, in the same month, the
virtual-cell manifesto, the AI-agents-in-oncology piece, three drug-repurposing
foundation models ([39322717](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39322717/), [39448863](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39448863/)) and a harms toolbox. The
enthusiasm and the audit are not separated in time anywhere in this corpus once
the window is wide enough to check, and every claim this corpus has made about a
lag between them has been withdrawn.

!!! note "What 2024 was for"
    Twelve months were added to test five "first appearance" claims. All five
    moved earlier, and eight of thirteen threads now open in 2024-01 — the first
    month that exists. The correct reading of that is not that 2024 was where
    things started. It is that this instrument cannot date beginnings, only
    floors, and it should stop trying.
